incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: runtime OOM observed on cluster-3a GPUs (p95 latency spikes). Priority: P1. Auto-created incident thread. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/runtime-oom

maya (oncall): taking this. brief status: customer-facing endpoints /v1/chat are seeing 503s intermittently. I’m on a CR.

priya (support): multiple customers reported errors starting ~14:12 UTC, ticket numbers: #8421, #8424. Impact: short-lived request failures, retry succeeds for many, but some large-batch jobs failing consistently.

ash (sre): logs show repeated OOMs inside the runtime worker process before the node reboots. Attaching clipped logs below.

logbot: ```
[14:12:07] runtime-worker-7 ERROR OOM: allocator failed to reserve 512MB for KV cache growth
[14:12:07] runtime-worker-7 INFO active_batches=28, avg_seq_len=1024, model=redwood-2b-quant, gpu_mem_used=15.8GB/16GB
[14:12:08] runtime-worker-7 ERROR gpu_oom_kv_pagewalk: failed to pin page 0x7f...
[14:12:09] runtime-worker-7 INFO evicted_pages=0 last_eviction_ms=0
[14:12:10] runtime-worker-7 WARN fallback_to_cpu=false
```

carlos (eng-runtime): hypothesis 1: KV cache growth + long sequences causing fragmentation + contiguous allocation failures. hypothesis 2: a memleak in batch accumulation path when prefix caching hits high cardinality.

devon (runtime): +1 on fragmentation. nvidia-smi dump from affected GPU attached:```
Tue Mar 15 14:12:09 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.60.13    Driver Version: 525.60.13    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
| Fan  Temp  Perf Pwr:Usage/Cap| Memory-Usage | GPU-Util | Processes:                                 |
|  34%   72C    P2   180W / 250W | 15809MiB / 16384MiB | 98%     |  python(12345)                              |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

maya (oncall): live mitigation applied: 1) scaled down concurrency on pool cluster-3a from 8 -> 4, 2) emergency route fallback to redwood-1b-quant in region eu-west as overflow path, 3) triggered forced small batch (batch_size=2) via runtime-config toggle for hot routes. Observed immediate drop in OOMs but p99 latency goes up slightly.

ash (sre): noted customer impact: 37 failed requests/min at peak, mostly for requests with sequence lengths > 800 and client-side batch sizes >= 16. Priya, can you confirm which customers had the large-batch jobs?

priya (support): confirmed: customer A (ingest pipeline) and customer C (embedding large docs) had the heavy tail. I've informed them and opened tickets for postmortem.

carlos (eng-runtime): sharing quick grep of recent deploys and config changes -- nothing in the last 48h except a kernel bump on infra-hosts (kmod 5.18 -> 5.19) which shouldn't affect user-space alloc but flagging anyway.

devon (runtime): current in-thread hypotheses to track: 
- H1: KV cache prefix churn causes small allocs that fragment GPU heap, preventing large contiguous blocks -> OOM on large batches.
- H2: Batch accumulation bug causing stale KV pointers incrementally increasing reserved memory.
- H3: Change in kernel or driver caused different page allocation behavior under pressure.

maya (oncall): for each hypothesis, we need reproducible checks and logs:
- H1 checks: per-request KV cache growth traces, histogram of allocation sizes, number of evictions.
- H2 checks: runtime metrics for batch-accumulator queue length, retained references.
- H3 checks: correlate incidents with nodes that had the kernel bump.

ash (sre): I dumped allocator internals from one crashed worker (core dump parsed): ```
allocator: free_segments=12 total_free=512MB largest_free=28MB
alloc_requests: 1024 failed_requests=7
kv_cache_map: entries=120k active_prefixes=18k
```
This suggests fragmentation: largest free chunk 28MB while we attempted ~512MB allocations.

carlos (eng-runtime): good catch. Immediate mitigations we can do (short-term):
- enable aggressive KV eviction policy for cluster-3a (evict cold prefixes after 30s)
- enable small-block pooling to avoid large contiguous allocations for KV structures (hot patch config, no code change)
- reduce default batch_size cap for hot routes from 32 -> 8

maya (oncall): please make the config changes and roll to cluster-3a. Ash, coordinate a controlled rollout to avoid cascading.

ash (sre): starting rolling config change now. Plan: patch 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 8 minutes, watch OOM metrics and p95/p99. If OOMs continue, force siphon traffic to fallback region for heavy routes.

logbot: config-change event recorded: `runtime.kvcache.eviction.sweep_sec=30` `runtime.batch.cap=8` `runtime.kvpool.small_pool=true`

(3 minutes later)

ash (sre): after first 30% rollout: OOM count down 65% in affected pool but p99 latency still elevated for some flow. No node reboots since rollout started.

devon (runtime): added a low-overhead diagnostic to collect per-alloc size histogram for 20 minutes on sampled workers (1/100 requests) to validate fragmentation hypothesis. Will share export when done.

lina (cust-suc): update to customers: we’ve applied mitigations and reduced failures substantially. We’ll follow up with a detailed RCA. Customers appreciate the quick response but want ETA for permanent fix.

maya (oncall): next actions / owners: 
- devon: gather allocator histograms & attach to thread (ETA 20m).
- carlos: review code paths for batch accumulation edge cases (ETA 2h).
- ash: complete post-incident timeline + handoff to infra for kernel correlation (ETA 1h).
- priya/lina: customer comms and tickets updated.

carlos (eng-runtime): small note: can we capture per-model memory maps? If H1 true, model KV layout matters (larger KV entries for redwood-2b-quant).

devon (runtime): started histogram sampling now. snippet of the histogram format I’ll post into the thread when finished to avoid massive logs.

(20 minutes later)

devon (runtime): histogram sample pasted: ```
alloc_size_bins: [0-4KB: 40% | 4KB-64KB: 35% | 64KB-1MB: 18% | 1MB-8MB: 6% | >8MB: 1%]
largest_free_chunk_hist: [<32MB: 78% of samples | 32-128MB: 20% | >128MB: 2%]
kv_prefix_growth_samples: avg_new_entries_per_request=12 median=6 tail_95=110
```

carlos (eng-runtime): that lines up with fragmentation theory: most free chunks under 32MB while large allocations requested occasionally. H1 gains strength.

ash (sre): conclusion for in-incident RCA: primary cause appears to be heap fragmentation aggravated by KV cache growth on long-seq large-batch requests. Secondary factors: driver/kernel behavior might have reduced ability to coalesce pages under high pressure; we need infra correlation.

maya (oncall): final live-mitigation notes: cap batch_size, enable small-block pool, and aggressive KV eviction. This restored service. We’ll schedule a deeper fix:
- medium-term: change KV allocator to favor large contiguous regions for model-critical allocations and implement threshold-based compaction.
- long-term: add online compaction & smarter placement across GPU memory pools; add stronger per-request KV limits and better backpressure to clients.

priya (support): customers notified with temporary workaround summary. They requested a timeline for permanent fix; I told them ETA will be provided after eng review.

ash (sre): tagging infra for kernel correlation: @infra-team -- please correlate host kernel/driver versions for nodes in cluster-3a that had OOMs between 14:00-14:30 UTC and report back.

incident-bot: Incident marked as mitigated at 14:38 UTC. Creating follow-up RCA doc.

maya (oncall): handing off to CARLOS/DEVON for RCA write-up and to ASH for post-incident timeline. I’ll be on stand-by for customer asks.

(reacted with :thumbsup: from carlos, ash)
